ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha e01faa1367fa (2026-05-12T14:13:20Z) modified collector/otelcol-config.yml and introduced a gRPC keepalive policy for the otel-collector that set max_connection_idle=60s. The AWS Network Load Balancer sitting in front of otelcol:4317 also has a 60-second idle TCP timeout. Because the NLB silently kills idle TCP connections at exactly 60s without sending a TCP RST visible to both sides before the gRPC PING keepalive fires, the collector repeatedly receives broken connections, triggers a goroutine enforcement loop ('max_connection_idle exceeded repeated enforcement loop'), and ultimately crashes (FATAL at 14:25:12). cart-service cannot reconnect because otel-collector is down, causing all OTLP gRPC exports to fail with 'connection refused' and the circuit breaker to open. Cart-service itself (Redis, business logic) remains fully healthy — only telemetry export is disrupted.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: restart the otel-collector pod to restore telemetry ingestion. 2. In collector/otelcol-config.yml (introduced in e01faa1367fa), increase grpc.keepalive.server_parameters.max_connection_idle to at least 90s (e.g., 120s) so it is comfortably longer than the NLB's 60s idle timeout. 3. Alternatively, configure the cart-service gRPC client keepalive_time to 20s and keepalive_timeout to 10s so a PING is sent before the NLB silently drops the connection, keeping the connection alive. 4. Set the NLB idle timeout to 350s (recommended for gRPC) via the AWS console to permanently prevent the mismatch. Deploy the config fix and confirm otel-collector stays up and cart-service exports resume without dropped spans.
